units.position: Rice Point's region metres: centre (0, 0), 760 x 360 m (x -380..380, y -180..180); x metres east, y metres north, both ground metres
units.world: in the game's world units (ADR 0034) x is the same and a metre of ground northward is 0.643 of a unit (world y = 0.643 x y); every y in this file is ground metres, and so are heights and sizes

offset.rule: Nine Mile Creek's metres: x_nmc = x - 760, y_nmc = y - 100. Rice Point's east edge (x 380) is Nine Mile Creek's west edge (x -380); the regions' south edges both lie at Nine Mile Creek's y -280

units.height: metres about mean sea level; spring low -2.20, neap low -0.99, mean 0, neap high +0.99, spring high +2.20
units.profile: cross-shore profiles are [distance from the reference line in metres, + inland, elevation in metres]
units.slope: a slope 1:n is n metres across for every metre of rise
units.wharf: the wharf's own frame (wharf.frame) places its parts: (u, v) is root + u x u_dir + v x v_dir; every point here is already in region metres
units.texture: ground/RicePointSeabed_HeightTex_plan.png: 16-bit grey, 1520 x 720, 2 texels a metre, texel (col, row) from the top-left centred at x = -380 + (col + 0.5) / 2, y = 180 - (row + 0.5) / 2; height = -6 + 12 x code / 65535. ground/RicePointSeabed_StillTex_plan.png: the still water on the same scale, code 0 = none (filter the codes, then decode: ADR 0046 s5)
units.stages: stage 0 is today: the textures. Stages 1 to 3 are the growth's plans, each marked later; their numbers are measured on the composer's ground for that stage (tools/rptGround.js), not on a texture
units.boats: a berth's bed is the shallowest on its keel line; afloat_from = bed + draught; way_in_from = the least bed from the open sea + draught; springs and neaps = the share of a spring (amplitude 2.2) or neap (0.99) tide's cycle when both hold

tide.rule: St Peters' tide, as Nine Mile Creek's: regions that share ground share a tide

nmc.meets: Nine Mile Creek's west edge from its y -280 to 80

seam.rule: Rice Point's column 1519 (x 379.75) carries Nine Mile Creek's column 0 (its x -379.75) code for code, in the height texture and the still texture; Rice Point's row r is Nine Mile Creek's row r + 400

measured.what: step: Rice Point's columns 1519 against 1518; kink: the slope across them against Nine Mile Creek's from column 0 to 1 (metres a metre)

sections.name: the back shore
sections.type: sand beach under marram dunes, open to the south-west
sections.why: The point's weather side: a dune ridge (+4.95) with a swale behind it (+4.35), a wide beach and a gently shelving sand bottom. The surf beach; the back shore camp stands in the swale. It runs on past the west edge, unbuilt.

sections.name: the point's west face
sections.type: shingle beach under a red bank 3 m tall
sections.why: Where the point takes the south-westerlies: a steep red sandstone bank and a shingle beach, the ledges running out from it. Its bottom falls away faster than the back shore's, so the sea edge off it is open water.

sections.name: the point's tip
sections.type: a low red bank over sandstone ledges
sections.why: Rice Point itself: a low bank, a narrow beach and a rock platform that bares at spring lows, the ledges fanning south-west from it.

sections.name: the lee shore
sections.type: stony beach under a red bank, in the point's lee
sections.why: The wharf's shore, sheltered by the point from the west and by the bar from the south. The bank top (+4.45 to +5.0) takes the yard; the gut runs close along it.

sections.name: the cove head
sections.why: The marsh platform (mostly +1.0 to +2.0) between the bank and the flats, over the neap highs and drowned by the spring highs; the brook winds across it to the cove.

sections.name: the cove's east shore
sections.type: sand and mud beach under a low bank
sections.why: The cove's quiet side: a gentle beach of sand and mud, eelgrass below the low-water line, the cove house on the bank above.

sections.name: Rice Point Strand
sections.type: sand beach under a low red bank (Nine Mile Creek's coast.nmc_rice_point_strand, carried on)
sections.why: Nine Mile Creek's south-shore beach, its storm berm and its red bank, carried on west to the cove: the same profile, on the same reference line, so the beach crosses the seam unchanged. Clam flats at low water.

water.rule: the water's shapes in plan order: shoals, the gut, the ledges, today's silt; then the growth's dredging, each from its stage on (stage), today's silt until its stage (until)

shapes.name: the bar
shapes.why: A sand bar from the strand's lower beach west across the cove's mouth to the gut. It shelters the cove and the wharf from the south, and it dries at the spring lows: the bar walk.

shapes.name: the ebb shoal
shapes.why: The sand the ebb carries out of the gut, lying across its mouth from the ledges to the bar's tip. The gut crosses it at its sill.

shapes.name: the gut
shapes.why: The tide's way in and out of the cove, scoured between the point's lee and the bar's tip: deepest (-5.75, the hole) right off the wharf's face, shoaling to its sill (-2.6) where it crosses the ebb shoal, and dying away inside the cove.

shapes.name: the point ledges
shapes.why: Five sandstone ledges running south-west off the point, their heads baring at the spring lows: lobster and crab ground, and the reason boats round the point wide.

shapes.name: the face's silt
shapes.why: The face was dredged when the wharf was worked and has silted back since it fell idle: a level bed at -2.0, eased into the gut over 4 m, so the face dries at the bottom of the spring lows. Dredged again at stage 1.

shapes.name: the inner berth's silt
shapes.why: Mud in the angle between the approach and the head. Dredged into the float basin at stage 2.

shapes.name: the end crib's spill
shapes.why: Stone from the south end's failed crib, spilled at its foot to -0.9. Cleared when the crib is rebuilt at stage 1.

shapes.name: the face berth, dredged
shapes.why: The face dredged to -4.1: the inshore boats (draught to 1.45 m) afloat at every tide with 0.45 m under them at the spring low.

shapes.name: the cut through the ebb shoal
shapes.why: The gut's sill cut to -4.0, 16 m wide, from the gut to the bay's own -4.0: the inshore boats cross at every tide.

shapes.name: the end berth, dredged
shapes.why: The south end dredged to -4.1 for the staffed second boat, afloat at every tide; dredged out to the gut, so the end is 24 m long when the head is widened at stage 3.

shapes.name: the float basin
shapes.why: The inner berth dredged to -3.4 for a float: skiffs, punts, dories and the open lobster boat afloat at every tide, the hardtop lobster boats and the Cape Islander at all but the bottom of the spring lows.

shapes.name: the deep berth
shapes.why: Along the widened head's new face, into the gut's own deep water: -5.7: the side dragger and the big sport fisher lie afloat at every tide, and cross the -4.0 sill at all but the bottom of the spring lows.

streams.name: the brook
streams.why: Out of the brook pond, south down a wooded valley, under Route 91 by a culvert and across the cove head's marsh to the cove.

mouth.into: the cove, at the marsh's seaward edge (fishing.rpt_brook_mouth)
mouth.what: bed: the brook's own bed (its last z); ground: the texture there, lower, where the cove's floor takes the brook

head_of_tide.rule: where the brook's bed rises over the spring high (+2.2): above it the brook is fresh at every tide

level.rule: the brook's water stands its depth over its bed (still water, ADR 0046) from its head to where the sea takes it (level -2.1 and below)

fishing: the brook mouth (fishing.rpt_brook_mouth): bass on the ebb; the spring runs (proposals)

ponds.name: the brook pond
ponds.why: A spring pond on the farmland, at the brook's head: brook trout, and skating in winter.

ponds.name: the marsh panne
ponds.why: A salt pool on the marsh platform, kept at +1.82 by its lip between the spring highs that fill it.

pools.rule: Still water in the ledges' hollows (ADR 0046). Each pool is a bowl cut into its ledge inside its outline, from `edge` m under its level at the outline down to its bed `reach` m in; cut only, and only there: every texel outside keyscene.rpt_point_ledges's box is the first issue's. Its water stands at its level over the ground inside the outline, and one texel beyond. Every tide covers it (its rim lies below the neap high) and refills it; every ebb leaves it standing (its level lies above the neap low).

call.lean: the pools go into Rice Point's still texture at part 1's next issue (still water lying in the ledges' hollows, filled by every tide and left by the ebb)

roads.name: Route 91
roads.builder: ThroughRoad (Nine Mile Creek's builder, carried on)

joins.heading: about 11 degrees south of west at the seam, as Nine Mile Creek's last segment runs (its (-373, -140.6) to (-380, -142)); "Rice Point's region takes the bend" (call 60)

ends.what: the end of Route 91: its asphalt stops at the turning circle's north-west edge, on the wharf's yard

turning.what: where a vehicle turns: an 18 m circle on the yard

measured.rule: the road's grade against today's texture along its centre line; where the ground lies within 0.12 m of the grade it stands (the bed's keep), so up to 0.12 is by design

roads.why: The one road in. From the seam it bends west behind the strand's bank top and the farm, crosses the brook by a culvert, passes north of the cove head's marsh and runs south-west down the point to the wharf, where it ends.

paths.name: the strand

joins.what: Nine Mile Creek's south-shore beach walk carries on here

paths.note: the beach itself, from the seam west along the strand and the cove's east shore to the cove head: walkable along its upper beach at every tide but the spring highs, when the berm takes it

paths.name: the bar walk
paths.note: out along the bar's crest from the strand's lower beach to the bar's tip at the gut: dry only near the bottom of a spring ebb (the crest -0.85 to -1.6)

paths.name: round the point

leaves.to: the back beach, running on unbuilt

paths.note: down the bank from the yard's south corner, along the lee beach, round the tip on its rock platform (half tide and below) and west along the back beach to the region's edge

wharf.name: the wharf at Rice Point (its own name stays open)
wharf.status: unused: nobody works it, its power is off

frame.how: a point (u, v) in the wharf's frame is root + u x u_dir + v x v_dir: u runs out from the shore, east-south-east; v along it, north-north-east

wharf.built: a timber crib wharf: stone-filled log cribs under a plank deck, an approach across the beach to a head along the gut

deck.what: the head's deck, 1.2 m above the spring high; the approach ramps from the yard's +4.0 to +3.4

cribs.name: the approach
cribs.state: sound; its deck planks grey, a few gone

cribs.name: the head
cribs.state: the north and middle cribs sound; the south crib failed, its stone spilled at the end (spill.rpt_end_crib)

yard.what: the yard on the bank top, where Route 91 ends

turning.what: where a vehicle turns: an 18 m circle on the yard, the asphalt ending at its north-west edge

road_end.what: Route 91's asphalt ends here, at the turning circle's edge: the end of the road

slip.surface: concrete planks on the beach, broken below mean
slip.what: a launching slip for small boats, 22 m north of the approach, from the bank top to below the neap low

ladders.today: standing; its rungs gone below about +0.5

bollards.rule: timber bollards along the face and the end every 8 m: five stand today, two have rotted to stumps

sheds.name: the old store
sheds.today: boarded; shingled, its sign gone; a dead power mast at its north corner
sheds.stage1: reopened: the wharf's store and office

sheds.name: the head shed
sheds.today: a gear shed with half its roof gone
sheds.stage1: rebuilt as the wharf's gear shed

lamps.rule: two lamp posts on the approach and one on the head; dark today (the power is off), lit from stage 1

berths.rule: a berth is a face a boat lies alongside; its bed is read along its keel line, 2.5 m off the face (fenders and half a beam) and 2 m in from each end: the shallowest bed on that line says from what tide each boat lies afloat there

list.name: the face

list.name: the end

list.name: the inner berth

calls.call: Rice Point's region: 760 x 360 m (x -380..380, y -180..180; 1520 x 720 texels), wider than tall (2.1 to 1). Its east edge meets Nine Mile Creek's west edge from Nine Mile Creek's y -280 to 80, 360 of its 560 m; the two regions' south edges line up, so the bay's floor runs straight across. x_nmc = x - 760, y_nmc = y - 100.
calls.lean: Take it: the strand, Route 91 and the farm cross the seam inside it, and its south edge is Nine Mile Creek's.

ruled.words: I go with all your leans

calls.topic: the wharf: where it stands, which way it faces, its depths, today's boats
calls.call: A timber crib wharf on the point's lee shore: a 38 m approach across the beach from the yard (+4.0) to a 12 x 38 m head (deck +3.4) along the gut, its face looking 118 degrees (east-south-east) into the gut's deep water. Today the face's bed is -2 (silted), the end's -0.9 (the failed crib's spill), the inner berth's -0.881; the way in crosses -2.62 at the gut's sill. No boat lies there today: by depth, the face floats a dory from -1.7, the lobster boat from -0.7 and the Cape Islander from -0.6; the side dragger only from 0.9.
calls.lean: Take the site: the deep water is the gut's, so the growth dredges little, and the point and the bar shelter it.

ruled.words: I go with all your leans

calls.call: Three stages, each marked later: 1, take it back (the face to -4.1 and a cut through the sill to -4.0: the inshore boats at the face and on the way in at every tide); 2, a staffed second boat (the end to -4.1, a float basin at -3.4, the trap yard, the bait shed, the crew in the wharf house); 3, the fleet (the head widened 12 m, a deep berth at -5.7, fuel, the cold store, a railway on the slip, three staff houses).
calls.lean: Take the three. A fourth, for the stern trawlers and the packet (beds of -6.5 and below, and a channel cut through the bay's -4 floor), is not proposed: it needs ground below -6 (call 9).

ruled.words: I go with all your leans

calls.call: 10 areas, each different: the strand flats, the bar, the cove, the gut, the wharf, the point ledges, the back shore, the brook mouth, the brook pond, the outer bay. All ten species are fished somewhere; other species are proposals only.
calls.lean: Take all ten areas, and add region.rice_point to every species' RegionIds. The proposals (smelt, gaspereau, eel, sea-run and brook trout, lumpfish, blue mussel, razor clam, an oyster and mussel lease, a dip net) wait for the owner.

calls.topic: Route 91's line, and where it ends
calls.call: From the seam at (380, -42) (Nine Mile Creek's (-380, -142)) Route 91 bends west behind the strand's bank top and the farm, crosses the brook by a culvert, passes north of the cove head and runs south-west down the point to the wharf. It ends at the yard's turning circle (18 m, gravel, +4.05) at (-109.7, -61.2). Three gravel lanes leave it (the farm lane north, the point lane and the back shore lane west).
calls.lean: Take it: the road ends at the wharf, so the wharf is the end of the road.

calls.topic: past the west and north edges
calls.call: West: the back beach, its dune and the point pasture run on past the edge, unbuilt, with the open sea off them. The edge's sea part (y -179.75 to -110.75) is the back shore's open sand bottom (-4.018 to -2.216), no bar, ledge or channel on it; the shore crosses the edge as plain beach (y -110.25 to -43.75). South: the open bay along Nine Mile Creek's own south edge (-4.345 to -2.906); the steering line into the gut starts on it in open water, and no stage of the growth changes either sea edge. North: farmland and woods at +6.0, no road.
calls.lean: Nothing built beyond either edge: the back beach is the region's wild edge. The shore must leave the frame somewhere; it leaves by the west edge on a plain stretch of beach, as the strand leaves by the seam, never across a point, a mouth or a channel (the brief, section 1).

calls.topic: the bluff's taper at the seam
calls.call: Nine Mile Creek's third issue laid its south shore (a +6.0 plateau, a bluff to +2.3 at its y -166 to -170, a +2.2 berm from its y -170 to -186) and feathered it back to its first issue's strand profile at its west edge, so its column 0 keeps the strand's gentle bank. Seen from Rice Point, the strand's bank turns into that bluff over its berm within 8 to 12 m east of the seam: the 2.3 m contour runs from y -83.25 at the seam to y -70.25 by x 390. A: leave it. B: Rice Point mirrors the bluff west of the seam and eases it out. C: Nine Mile Creek's next issue carries its bluff to its column 0, and Rice Point takes it up.
calls.lean: A. Nine Mile Creek is ruled and the seam holds code for code; the taper is Nine Mile Creek's own, and part 2's strand board shows it. B would leave a 16 m notch at the seam, where both regions keep the strand's bank; C moves the column the brief holds fixed, so only on the owner's word.
